note: Every value below was read from the deployed revision or the live cluster. It contains no credentials.

surfaces_agree.claim: the sweep, the per-pair verdict and the agent's evidence resolve one pair identically

inherited_general.why: the master already violates, so the rendition introduced nothing

persisted_pair.why: submitted through /v1/scan rather than the catalogue; must resolve through the same anti-join

parity.claim: sql/006_catalogue_regression.sql and safe_frame.detector implement the same published rule
parity.verified_against: the live self-hosted cluster through the official mcp-clickhouse stdio transport
parity.runs_in_ci: the `parity` job stands up a throwaway ClickHouse and runs all 46 on every commit; it fails if they skip
plus: red alternation under the luminance floor: red_flash only
four red and four luminance transitions in one second: neither rule fires
parity.defect_this_found: these tests needed a cluster, CI had none, so all 45 skipped everywhere and the green run read as a pass. Under that cover the parametrized case compared the SQL's first row against the detector's whole result list and could never have passed. The implementations did agree once the comparison was corrected -- but nothing had demonstrated it until now.

query_shape_benchmark.question: one scan with ARRAY JOIN fan-out, or two scans unioned
query_shape_benchmark.measured_against: the 9,600,000-row corpus, before the measured cohort was added; not re-measured since, and the shape of the result is unchanged
query_shape_benchmark.result: identical 44-row output at the time of measurement; the single-scan form is 27% slower
query_shape_benchmark.why: two passes read 10.26M rather than 19.2M because per-granule min/max lets ClickHouse skip ~93% of the second scan, so the extra scan is nearly free

notes: The catalogue is self-authored synthetic measurement, not footage, and contains no flashing media.
This is an open pre-check and never claims device or regulatory certification.

design_acceptance.method: scripts/visual_check.py drives a real browser; --offline needs no cluster
asserted: no horizontal page scroll at any width in either theme
no console errors or uncaught exceptions on the judge path
initialisation completes with the backend entirely absent
a failing sweep reports failing closed rather than throwing
the evidence path completes: sweep, selection, timeline, draw, caption, table view

series_palette.validated_with: the dataviz palette validator, against this page's own surfaces
series_palette.note: colour is never the only cue; every rule mark is paired with its name

accessibility: skip link, visible focus rings, keyboard-selectable result rows
the chart carries an aria-label stating the finding, plus a table view of the same numbers
all transitions disabled under prefers-reduced-motion; no looping animation anywhere
no flashing or moving media on a page about flashing media
the visitor's OS colour preference is honoured; an explicit choice overrides it both ways

defects_found_by_this_check: a `let` read from its temporal dead zone during theme restore threw at init and detached every listener; the page rendered and did nothing, and the whole pytest suite passed
the chart placeholder was a child of the element the draw replaces, so every successful draw destroyed it and then threw, silently skipping the caption, table view and tooltip
the phone card layout had width:100% plus margins and overflowed the viewport by exactly the margin

the SQL/Python parity test -- cited as the proof that the catalogue sweep and the per-file detector cannot disagree -- had never executed: it was skipped in every environment, and its comparison was malformed in both branches

the persistent mcp-clickhouse worker was cached per configuration but its queue, lock and task belong to one event loop; a second loop in the same process raised 'Event loop is closed'. The service runs one loop and never hit it, so only a test suite could

multi_step_agent.note: every tool is a live query through the official mcp-clickhouse server; the trace is recorded from the run and returned with the brief

systemic_finding.why_it_matters: 66 findings resolve to four encoder profiles with two distinct root causes, so the action is a handful of upstream fixes rather than 66 patches; 23 are invisible to a luminance-only checker

on_the_page: who it is for, named in one line under the hero
the impact case with its sources
the live sweep, and the evidence chart for any finding
the systemic cause: every transform with its regression rate and rule split
the multi-step agent brief with the tool sequence it actually ran
the partner integration, checkable in place: transport, read-only status, advertised tools and a live query result
the runtime hops with the credential boundary marked
every threshold traced to its published definition, including the one not implemented
an export so the findings can leave the page
a check of your own video, decoded in the browser and never displayed
a self-serve API key, and the calls to use it

standards_audit.why: expert review could not be obtained; the implementation was audited against the primary texts instead
defects_found: relative luminance was not linearised before applying the BT.709 coefficients
the general-flash darker-image condition (<0.80) was missing entirely
saturated red used R - max(G,B) rather than the published R/(R+G+B) >= 0.8 test
red-transition direction was taken from the luminance signal, recording a matched-luminance red alternation as flat
deviations_remaining: area is a frame fraction, not the angular 25% of a 10 degree visual field (matches Ofcom/ITU and every guideline except WCAG)
concurrent flashes are not composited; the peak changed area across the window is used
the synthetic corpus authors its metrics rather than measuring pixels
the spatial-pattern rule is not implemented
standards_audit.not_equivalent_to: review by a qualified photosensitive-epilepsy or broadcast professional

public_api_exposure.no_api_key: deliberate: judging requires the product to be testable without an account
public_api_exposure.writes: /v1/scan only; identifiers belonging to the published catalogue are refused, so an anonymous write cannot suppress a documented finding
public_api_exposure.samples: /v1/samples mints a unique lineage per request so callers cannot collide
public_api_exposure.rate_limits: per client per minute on /v1/scan, /v1/triage and /v1/explain; no read endpoint is capped
public_api_exposure.mcp: read-only, ClickHouse credentials only, SELECT-only database user

measured_cohort.why: every other row is an authored number; nothing at scale ran the measurement stage
measured_cohort.how: constructed RGB frame sequences pushed through safe_frame.ingest.frames_to_transitions, so every value is the output of relative_luminance and red_flash_mask over real pixel arrays
measured_cohort.result: precision and recall 1.000 on the measured cohort, identical to the authored one
measured_cohort.note: the frames are constructed, not filmed, and none is ever rendered or displayed

bring_your_own_clip.why: every other surface runs on a catalogue we chose, which a judge can fairly discount
bring_your_own_clip.how: the browser decodes the file to raw RGB on a small grid and posts only those samples; measurement stays in safe_frame.ingest so there is no second implementation of the published maths
bring_your_own_clip.never_displayed: the video element is created but never inserted into the document, so a clip somebody is checking because they suspect it flashes is never painted on a page about photosensitive seizures
bring_your_own_clip.never_uploaded: the file itself does not leave the machine

modes.absolute: rendition alone, criteria evaluated over inline rows, writes nothing
modes.regression: rendition plus approved master, the child-only anti-join this product exists for

bring_your_own_clip.grid: longest edge reduced to 48 cells; stated on every result
bring_your_own_clip.why_that_grid_is_enough: the published area condition is a proportion of the screen (0.25), which a grid this size resolves; a flash too small for it does not meet the area condition anyway

api_keys.optional_by_design: every endpoint works with no credential at exactly the limits it had before keys existed, because the submission must be testable without an account
api_keys.what_a_key_buys: 5x the per-minute cap on the endpoints that spend model tokens or write, and the caller named in the logs; reads are uncapped either way
api_keys.stateless: an identifier and an issue date signed with an HMAC held in Secret Manager, so there is no credential table, no write on the request path, and nothing lost on restart
api_keys.stated_limitation: an individual key cannot be revoked without rotating the signing secret; this is printed on the key itself, and keys expire after 90 days
edge_cases_refused_with_a_reason: key signed with a different secret
api_keys.not_silently_downgraded: a present-but-broken credential is refused, so a caller learns why their quota did not rise
api_keys.hosting_quirk_documented: a POST with no Content-Length is rejected with 411 by the load balancer before it reaches the service, so curl needs an explicit empty body
